findings.reason: co-location of writer and reader is not a property the plan establishes, and coordinators, review workers and the station routinely run on different nodes, so a worker implementing this exactly as written replaces a slow scan with a read path that silently hides every cross-node review record; the section needs a shared index location, or a cheap cross-node freshness probe over the store, or a stated co-location and staleness bound that a rebuild can enforce.
findings.text: §45 makes the persisted index version the sole freshness signal ("checks freshness by comparing that version, without listing or stat-ing the store"), but that document is filed through `cache_document_path` into `node_local_cache_dir`, which `reckon/crew/review_records.py:1167` describes as sitting "where this node's processes all see it and no other node does", while the review store it indexes is on the shared home; a record stored by a process on another node therefore moves the store without advancing this node's index version, and none of the stated rebuild triggers — missing, unreadable, stamped by other code — fires, so the reader never sees that record at all.

findings.reason: the node can satisfy its whole measure while the defect the section exists to remove survives in the one path that matters, so the done-when must read through the station's refresh (as §43's does) or the deliverable must say the tick-store path stops bypassing the writer index.
findings.text: the done-when reads "every run's records" through an ordinary lookup, but `_store_indexes` returns `_build_store_indexes` — a from-scratch listing and parse of the whole store — whenever `_TICK_REVIEW_STORES` is installed (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:1631`), and §43, which §45 declares it depends on, is exactly the section that installs that per-tick store in the station's refresh; so the refresh path the Why measures at 5.6 s per tick keeps rebuilding from scratch and the new gate still passes on a direct read.
